en.title: GTA 5 Actor Slams Doubters Calling GTA 6 Too Similar
en.summary: Ned Luke, the voice of Michael De Santa in GTA 5, has strongly defended Rockstar's upcoming Grand Theft Auto 6 against claims that it looks too much like its predecessor. He believes critics are simply not paying close enough attention to the advancements made.
en.body:
The wait for Grand Theft Auto 6 has been an exercise in patience, with fans dissecting every trailer and leak with microscopic intensity. Following the extended look at Rockstar's next opus, a familiar debate has emerged: does GTA 6 look too much like GTA 5? Ned Luke, the actor who brought the complex character of Michael De Santa to life in 2013's Grand Theft Auto 5, has vocally dismissed these comparisons, asserting that such opinions are wildly misinformed.

Luke, a prominent and respected voice within the GTA community since GTA 5's release, recently shared his perspective on the matter. When asked about the sentiments suggesting a lack of visual or gameplay evolution between the two titles, he was unequivocal. "This looks nothing like Grand Theft Auto 5," Luke stated emphatically, adding, "I think they're out of their minds." He further quipped about his own appearance in the game, "I'll tell you one thing: I never looked that good," referencing the visual upgrades seen in the new protagonist, Jason.

## A New Era for Vice City

Rockstar Games has consistently pushed the boundaries of open-world design, and GTA 6 is no exception. While the core tenets of the Grand Theft Auto experience—a sprawling sandbox, compelling narrative, and a wealth of activities—remain, the underlying technology and presentation have been dramatically overhauled. The extended look showcased not only a vibrant, reimagined Vice City but also a host of new gameplay mechanics and systems designed to immerse players more deeply than ever before. From an overhauled Wanted system to a multitude of new side missions and interactive elements, the attention to detail is evident. Luke specifically pointed to the character animations as a key indicator of Rockstar's progress, suggesting that the way characters move and interact with the world represents a significant leap forward.

## Community Divided, Anticipation High

For many fans, the comparison point of GTA 5 is high praise, given its enduring popularity and critical acclaim nearly a decade and a half after its launch. However, the expectation for GTA 6 is not just a refinement but a revolution. The skepticism voiced by some, suggesting that the new installment might feel like a reskin, is a testament to the high bar set by both the franchise and Rockstar's own reputation for innovation. Ned Luke's defense serves as a powerful counterpoint, coming from someone who was intimately involved in the creation of the previous benchmark. His conviction suggests that the visual and mechanical differences are substantial, and perhaps only fully appreciable when experiencing the game firsthand. The passion from both the developers and their key collaborators like Luke underscores the immense care being poured into making GTA 6 a truly next-generation experience.

## What's Next

Rockstar Games has confirmed that Grand Theft Auto 6 is slated for release in 2025. Further details regarding specific platforms and a more precise release window are expected to be announced by the developer in the coming months as development progresses.

Luke has remained an important figure in the GTA community since he first appeared as one of three playable professional criminals in the 2013 installment. Now that he and the rest of the world have gotten a closer look at what Rockstar Games is cooking up with GTA 6, he's stepped in to defend it from the naysayers. One of the many, many talking points to emerge in the wake of last week's GTA 6: Extended Look was that playing as protagonists Jason and Lucia looked a little too similar to the kind of gameplay one could expect from GTA 5. While most seem to believe Rockstar has wisely used the 13 years since that game's release, it hasn't stopped skepticism from creeping in. Luke doesn't seem to be included in the new game's cast, but he still made sure to refute some of the criticisms popping up online while collaborating with YouTube channels Partychat and House of Highlights . When asked for his thoughts about those who believe there are too many similarities between GTA 5 and GTA 6, he made his stance clear. "This looks nothing like Grand Theft Auto 5," he said. "I think they're out of their minds." "I'll tell you one thing: I never looked that good," he added, pointing to an image of Jason on his screen." Rockstar's GTA 6 extended look officially revealed footage of a host of new features, including tons of new side activities , story missions , a reworked Wanted system , and more. For Luke, one of the best examples of how Rockstar has reimagined Grand Theft Auto can be seen in how its many characters move.
